plan:
- Design an inverted Pepper's Ghost configuration using an ultra-bright high-contrast display hidden inside a recess in the base to conceal the light source.
- Select a high-efficiency optical combiner glass with anti-reflective coating on the back surface, angling it precisely at 45 degrees to project the reservoir simulation.
- Integrate a single-board computer like a Raspberry Pi 5 to run the 3D reservoir simulation rendering pipeline and output to the hidden display.
- Construct a matte-black light-absorbing enclosure using CNC-routed MDF or 3D-printed parts to eliminate internal reflections and mask the glass edges.
- Install an addressable LED bezel or ambient backlight inside the chamber to control contrast and enhance the illusion of the model floating in mid-air.

originalPrompt: Create a reservoir simulation model using a hologram trick or Pepper's Ghost trick to project the model in the air without any visible glass or transparent material sheets

subSteps.title: Install heat-set inserts into chassis base

detail.tip: Keep the soldering iron completely perpendicular to the MDF board to prevent the brass inserts from setting at an angle, which could cause misalignment during bracket assembly.
steps: Locate the pre-drilled or CNC-routed mounting holes on the top surface of the Chassis Lower Base.
Clean out any wood dust or debris from the thirty mounting holes using a vacuum or compressed air.
Heat a soldering iron fitted with an M3-compatible brass insertion tip to 220°C.
Place an M3 Threaded Heat-Set Insert vertically over one of the chassis mounting holes.
Gently press the hot soldering iron tip into the center of the brass insert until it melts and sinks flush into the Chassis Lower Base.
Repeat the insertion process for all remaining twenty-nine mounting holes on the chassis base, ensuring each insert sits perfectly square.
detail.summary: Install thirty M3 brass heat-set inserts into the Chassis Lower Base.

projectDescription: An interactive holographic reservoir simulator projects dynamic 3D geological models in mid-air using a hidden laser projector and optical combiner. Powered by a main controller SBC and illuminated by custom chamber ambient backlighting, the system achieves a floating Pepper's Ghost illusion without any visible glass edges.
